subject: Recap + ask: Hosted API pricing qualification (monthly tokens + peak TPS)
messages:

Subject: Recap + ask: Hosted API pricing qualification (monthly tokens + peak TPS)

Hi Sofia / Tom —

Thanks again for the call earlier — good to learn more about Acme AI's summarization product and how you expect to use the hosted API. Quick recap and a couple of asks so we can put together a formal quote and a short trial plan: 

Recap:
- Use case: real-time document summarization for enterprise customers (latency-sensitive, multi-tenant).
- Typical request size: ~300 tokens in (prompt) / ~150 tokens out (summary) average.
- Important: predictable latency (SLO ~300ms tail for short summaries) and ability to handle bursts during business hours.

Asks (to finalize pricing/commit recommendation):
1) Expected monthly token volume (please include both prompt + completion tokens if possible).
2) Peak TPS (requests per second) you expect during bursts.
3) Target budget range and any target $/1M tokens you were hoping to hit for committed pricing.

We attached a small traffic_estimates.csv template — if you can drop numbers in there that would be perfect. Based on what you told us on the call, a rough working example is 80–120M tokens/month and a peak of ~5–10 TPS, but please correct this.

Next steps from our side once we have numbers:
- We’ll produce a pricing estimate (pay-as-you-go vs 6/12 month committed tiers) and show unit economics at your volumes.
- Propose a 30-day trial key and a simple mutual action plan (attach MMP) to validate latency and cost.

If you can reply with the numbers today/tomorrow we’ll aim to get a formal quote out within 24 hours.

Thanks!

—Alex Martinez
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Hi Alex —

Thanks for the clear recap. We filled out the CSV and included some additional notes inline. High-level answers below: 

- Expected monthly token volume (prompt + completion): ~100,000,000 tokens/month (we modeled 90–110M; 100M is our mid).
- Peak TPS: 8 TPS during North American business hours (with 1–2 hour spikes up to ~12 TPS during big customer syncs).
- Budget range: we're looking at $5k–$8k/month initially for hosted inference, with potential to expand if unit economics look good.
- Target $/1M tokens: our procurement team is hoping for ~ $60 / 1M tokens (this is flexible with committed discounts).

Two quick clarifying Qs: 
1) How does Redwood price prompt vs completion tokens (are they the same bucket)?
2) Do you have a recommended approach to guarantee tail latency for the spikes (do we need Reserved capacity or is hosted API with burst OK)?

We’re interested in a 30-day trial to validate latency and cost. Also please include any standard onboarding or whitelisting steps.

—Sofia
Head of Product, Acme AI
sofia@acmeai.com

From: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Alvarez <sofia@acmeai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-02T14:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap + ask: Hosted API pricing qualification (monthly tokens + peak TPS)

Thanks Sofia — this is perfect and very helpful. A few answers and a proposed pricing sketch based on the numbers you provided: 

About tokens: Redwood bills on total tokens (prompt + completion) as a single usage bucket. We show both in the usage UI but unit pricing is applied to the combined token count.

Latency/peaks: for the TPS profile you described (8 TPS baseline with spikes to ~12 TPS) the hosted API can usually accommodate bursts without a Dedicated plan, assuming you accept short warm-up tails. If you need hard SLOs for tail latency during spikes we typically recommend Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity) or a small committed burst block. For the trial we can provision a burst buffer and instrument KV/prefix caching so you can validate tail latency.

Pricing sketch (workable starting point):
- Pay-as-you-go: $80 / 1M tokens (no commitment).
- 6/12-month committed tier (100M/mo expected): $60 / 1M tokens (applies once commit threshold met; includes priority routing and modest discount on burst capacity).
- If you commit to 200M+/mo we can discuss an additional tier at ~$50 / 1M tokens.

Estimated monthly cost at your midpoint (100M tokens):
- Pay-as-you-go: ~$8,000/mo
- Committed (100M target at $60/1M): ~$6,000/mo

Notes on peak TPS and cost: handling bursts has a small cost uplift (we estimate ~+8–12% on effective cost if you need guaranteed headroom for spikes without Dedicated). We’ll model this in the formal quote.

Next steps I propose:
1) I’ll send a formal quote with line items for PAYG vs 6/12mo commit (including expected monthly cost and burst uplift).
2) We’ll provision a 30-day trial key and a small burst buffer so you can validate latency (no charge for the trial burst).
3) If you’re happy, we can convert the trial to a short-term commit and then to a longer reserve.

Ben — tagging you for any additional notes on contract/commit language.

—Alex Martinez
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
